_note: PURGED AND REBUILT 2026-08-23 (Ben): the hot file holds only the items of the earliest incomplete sprint - Sprint 16, the mercenary vertical slice (v0.1.15). Every item that existed before (530, ids <= BL-568) is snapshotted verbatim in archive/backlog-purged-2026-08-23.json and is NOT open work. New items name their sprint in `sprint`. File nothing here that the open sprint does not need; when the sprint closes, the next sprint's items are authored fresh against the authority docs. Ids never reuse.
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

items.title: A province has a holder, and a won battle moves it
condition_set can say 'province P held by the subject', and a contract template is an authored Lua row
items.summary: CONTRACTS.md's spine - a contract IS a condition_set the client will pay to have become true - cannot be expressed: the nine subjects are world-wide corp scalars with no location qualifier, and a condition_set holds a std::string key so it is not fixed-size or serialisable. This item appends subject province_held with a province qualifier on condition, measured against world::province_holder, and adds the authored contract-template table (scripts/contracts.lua) so a contract stores a template index plus bound operands, never a free condition_set.
items.design:
## Work

1. `condition_subject::province_held` (append-only; `condition_subject_count` bumps). `condition` gains `uint32_t province` (sentinel `no_province`). `measure_condition` returns 1 when `province_holder[province] == subject_corp`, else 0; comparator `>=` 1 is the 'hold' predicate. META_LAYER.md gets the tenth subject row.
2. `condition_text` renders it: 'holds <province name or #id>'.
3. `scripts/contracts.lua`: a template table `{ id, name, predicate = { subject, comparator, operand }, continuous, fee_mult, deadline_ticks }`. First two rows: **take** (province_held >= 1 at deadline) and **hold** (province_held >= 1 on every tick until deadline; `continuous = true`). Loaded through the existing sol2 registry path, protected calls only.
4. `condition_set_harness.cpp`: province_held measures correctly for holder / non-holder / sea province; the template table loads and round-trips its index.

## Rule carried
A new contract kind is a Lua row, not a C++ change (CONTRACTS.md). This item is what makes that true.

items.title: Nations field force: a garrison per nation, and a battle can have a nation on one side
items.summary: A contract offer is 'a campaign a polity wants and cannot win alone' - so the thing the company fights is the OTHER polity's force. Today nations own no units (the only owner assignment is corporation_generation.cpp:1245) and run_battles triggers only on corp_hostile_pairs. Without this item every contract resolves against nothing. Design-owed on two calls: how big a garrison is (anchor: NATIONS.md's value anchor - a unit's equipment costs twice its salary - and the nation's military_research line) and whether a nation garrison marches at all in this slice (proposed: no - garrisons are static defenders; a nation that wants ground hires).
items.design:
## Settled (Ben, elicitation, 2026-08-23)

1. **Garrison size.** Capital province + border provinces shared with the highest-grudge neighbour, count treasury-scaled (`nation_component::treasury`) against the value anchor (BL-543). Static this slice.
2. **Trigger.** `run_battles` gains a second trigger: a unit owned by a corp holding an ACTIVE contract whose target province is held by nation N engages N's garrison there. No `declare_hostile` row needed - the contract is the hostility. Nation-vs-corp pair state is a `stance` row keyed on the contract, cleared at terminal state.
3. **Upkeep.** YES - a `military_research`-line budget claim (the nation pays its own force).

Ratified into docs/military/MILITARY.md § Nation garrisons and docs/politics/NATIONS.md § A budget.

## Work
`unit_component::owner` accepts a nation entity; generation seeds garrisons; `run_battles` second trigger; `battle_engagement_harness` case: a corp-vs-nation battle opens and resolves; blackboard export lists garrisons as visible units (the competitor-visibility rule applies - count visible, internals private).

items.title: A nation derives a contract offer from its budget, and the contracted_force line takes a subject
items.summary: CONTRACTS.md says offers reuse history_sim's campaign scorer; the code says that scorer is an inline block in the Era -1 year loop over polity/region, unreachable from the campaign tick and typed on different data. So offer derivation is owed a design of its own, built on what IS live: score_national_budgets already pushes weight into budget_priority::contracted_force from the threat term (nation_ai.cpp:665), and the budget pass already earmarks a line's share as a whole-or-nothing claim. The shape: the contracted_force line's share funds an offer; the offer names the province; the fee is the earmark.
items.design:
## Settled (Ben, elicitation, 2026-08-23)

1. **Which province.** Among provinces held by the nation's highest-grudge neighbour (nation_score_terms.mean_grudge, border_force), the border province with the lowest garrison strength - deterministic argmin, ties by ascending province id.
2. **Fee.** The contracted_force line's spendable share this tick, accumulated across ticks into a dedicated `offer_escrow` until it clears the template's minimum (NR-572 showed a single-tick share cannot fund an indivisible claim; escrow is the answer, and it must be a visible treasury line). Deadline from the template.
3. **Cadence.** SEVERAL offers open concurrently (Ben's ruling, overriding the one-at-a-time proposal), one per threatened border province; each still expires independently after `offer_ttl_ticks`, returning its escrow. The concurrent-offer budget split - a tick's `contracted_force` share applied to open offers oldest-issued-first - is a call taken on Ben's behalf, since the elicitation settled cadence but not the split rule; flagged NR-576.

Ratified into docs/economy/CONTRACTS.md § Where offers come from and docs/politics/NATIONS.md § A budget. NR-572's income half (nations start at treasury 0, no levy enacted by default) is UNRESOLVED - this item closes the indivisibility half only.

## Work
`mercenary_offer{id, client, target_province, template, fee, deadline, issued_tick}`; `world::mercenary_offers` (a vector, not a scalar, now that offers are concurrent); `derive_contract_offers` called from `run_nation_step` after the budget pass; `line_takes_subject(contracted_force) = true` (the comment in nation_budget.hpp:127 names this as the extension); save section + version bump; `nation_scorer_harness` R5: a threatened nation issues an offer, an unthreatened one does not, two offers can be open and filling at once, and the sequence is replayable.

CONTRACTS.md's 'offers reuse the campaign scorer' line is amended by this item: the mechanism transfers (a want the polity cannot meet alone), the code does not - § Where offers come from now names the nation-budget-derived mechanism.

items.title: The mercenary contract: accept an offer with a named force, evaluate it each tick, pay or fail
items.summary: The record CONTRACTS.md specifies and procurement cannot express: a mercenary_contract with a template index, bound operands, a committed force, a deadline, and THREE terminal states (completed / failed / abandoned). Two append-only corp_verbs: accept_offer (offer id + unit ids) and abandon_contract. Payment rides the existing nation-to-corp budget_claim rail as a split payment: deposit at accept, remainder at completion; failure forfeits the remainder and folds a new sentiment_factor_kind::contract_failed - the 'down hardest' move CONTRACTS.md rules on.
items.design:
## Work

1. `mercenary_contract{id, client, contractor, template, province, fee, deposit_paid, deadline, accepted_tick, units[8], state}`; `world::mercenary_contracts`.
2. `corp_verb::accept_offer` / `corp_verb::abandon_contract` appended after `withdraw_from_battle`; `corp_command` reuses `counterparty` (validated against nations, not corps - the seam's counterparty check forks on verb) and gains `units`. Reject on: offer expired, unit not owned, unit already committed. A rejection mutates nothing (the untrusted-seam rule).
3. Evaluate in the economy tick after `run_battles`: `continuous` templates fail on the first tick the predicate is false; point templates test at the deadline. Completed -> remainder paid (budget_claim, contracted_force), `note_conduct(contract_completed)`. Failed -> `contract_failed` folded, escrow returned to the client. Abandoned -> as failed but the contractor chose it.
4. Committed units cannot be disbanded or re-committed; `march_unit` stays free (the player chooses how to use the force).
5. Save: section + version bump; `save_roundtrip` covers one open contract.
6. ACTIONS.json: two new gameplay entries transcribed from the seam (`render_actions.js` is the shape check).

## Settled already (CONTRACTS.md)
The player chooses the force; a contract is refusable; an offer is a nation's want; failure is the hardest reputation move.

items.title: One observed instance of every contract terminal state, conserved and replayable
items.summary: CONTRACTS.md demands one observed instance of each terminal state; no harness in the tree can observe any. This is the headless proof the slice rests on, in the procurement_harness.cpp pattern (fixture world, scripted verbs, bit-exact goldens).
items.design:
## Cases

M1 offer issued by a threatened nation; M2 accept with a valid force, deposit moves client->contractor and conserves exactly; M3 take-template completed on a decisive battle (BL-569/BL-571 fixtures), remainder paid; M4 hold-template failed on the first lost tick, escrow returned, `contract_failed` folded and reputation lower than after a cancel; M5 abandon; M6 two runs from one seed hash-identical across all of the above; M7 save/load mid-contract round-trips. Name the harness in the verifier-headless skill.

items.title: A unit is visible on the Planetary canvas and can be ordered to march
The Contracts ledger: offers in, accept with a force, active and past contracts
items.summary: The offer has to reach a human. No contract, offer, procurement or budget surface exists; the decision feed prints 'contract #n' and that is the whole story. A fold-out ledger in the nav rail with three views - Offers (client, province, fee, deadline, the client's visible garrison), Active (predicate text from condition_text, ticks left, committed force), History (terminal state, paid) - and an Accept flow that is a unit picker over the player's uncommitted units.
items.design:
## Work

1. Rail slot + `show_contracts_ledger`; the toggle rule (re-clicking the active tab closes).
2. Offers view rows; the Accept press opens the force picker (owned, uncommitted units with strength); confirm dispatches `accept_offer`. Decline is local (the offer stays until expiry - refusable, not dismissable).
3. Active view: `condition_text` line, deadline countdown, an Abandon press with the reputation cost shown.
4. Question-log entries (the question each view answers); ACTIONS.json ledger-family entries.
5. The fog rule: an offer is visible only if the target body is at least Known (DISCOVERY.md) - CONTRACTS.md's settled answer.

items.title: A contract announces itself: Public-channel messages, a card, and contract income in the budget
items.summary: An event lands with its message, in the same change (EVENTS.md's rule). Offer issued, accepted, completed, failed and abandoned each post to the Public channel through the existing session_history path; the battle card's sibling, a contract card, opens from the ledger; and the fee shows as a 'Contract income' line in the Balance ledger - budget_result::subsidies already carries it and nothing renders it.
items.design:
## Work

1. `economy_report::contract_events` -> `session_history::post_contract_events` -> Public channel; five phrasings in the dispatch-text bank.
2. `selection_kind::contract` card: client, predicate, force, deadline, fee split.
3. Balance ledger line 'Contract income' from `subsidies`; the header runway reads it.
4. Question-log entries for the card and the line.

items.title: The vertical slice plays end-to-end: hired, fought, paid - and v0.1.15 is cut
items.summary: Sprint 16's goal, verbatim: a polity hires the company, the company fights, the company is paid - playable end-to-end, however rough. This is the item-spanning requirement and the release: a scripted verifier-visual run from a new world through an accepted offer, a march, a battle card, a completed contract and the income line, plus a live playthrough by a human, then the v0.1.15 cut per DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md.
items.design:
## Done when

1. `scripts/verify/mercenary_slice.lua` captures: the ledger with an offer; the force picker; a unit marching; the battle card; a completed contract; Balance with contract income. All six captures inspected.
2. A live session reaches a paid contract without the agent protocol.
3. The determinism harness hash is unchanged for a world with no contract activity (the flag-off byte-identity rule).
4. v0.1.15 tagged; ROADMAP.md's done-definition for the minor met; MANUAL.md gains a Contracts section written from the shipped surfaces; the Sprint 16 retro is recorded in sprints.json.

items.title: a per-tick throughput RATE gates movement — bifold passive (trade, free) and active (military, credit-priced), generated by cities
items.summary: LOGISTICS.md names one reach field (BL-325 ruling 3) but no throughput cap on it: reach says a leg is admissible, nothing today says how much can move through it at once. This item builds Logistic Points — a per-tick RATE (never a stock; what carries over is goods moved, never points), generated by cities, split passive (ambient, serves the convoy layer that runs itself, free) and active (owned, militaries only, credit-priced). A leg over the cap is refused outright and the refusal is surfaced, never silently queued.
items.design:
## What settles this item

Almost entirely pre-argued: BL-464's archived design (archive/backlog-design-2026-Q3.json) carries three settled rules, seven satisfied constraints, and Ben's bifold ruling (2026-08-22) and refusal/surfacing ruling (2026-08-22, design register) verbatim. This item re-files it fresh per the 2026-08-23 purge policy — nothing here overturns the prior rulings, it promotes them to build.

## Shape

1. **Passive LP** — generated per city, drawn automatically by `supply_system.cpp` convoy dispatch. Free (already priced by haulage credits); LP only decides admissibility, never a second price (rule 1).
2. **Active LP** — generated per city, drawn only by `run_unit_march` (economy_system.cpp) for a marching unit's leg. Costs credits per unit-distance, argued against BL-543's value anchor rather than guessed — first-cut rate lands as a named constant in `scripts/economy.lua` § military, calibration not ruling (numbers are data, tuned in play like every other authored rate in this file).
3. **Locus.** LP lives on generated cities, never pooled per-corp — constraint 2, the exact abstraction `military_points` was deleted for. A rival can build the generator (port / inland hub) through the existing `corp_ai.cpp` candidate list, so the rate is not an asymmetric tax.
4. **Consumer order.** Adopts the existing NR-344/BL-472 ruling ("war flips the queue") as LP's answer too: at peace, passive (trade) claims a city's throughput first; a corp party to any declared hostility feeds active first that tick. One rule, already ratified, not reinvented here.
5. **Refusal.** A leg over the cap is rejected outright — no partial move, no silent queue — and the rejection is surfaced (a comms message, same convention as interdiction, LOGISTICS.md §7). Allocation under contention is a deterministic priority over a sorted set (ascending city id), never iteration order.
6. **No serialisation.** A rate crosses no tick boundary — no `state_hash` entry, nothing added to the save seam.

## Verification

`logistics_points_harness.cpp`: passive/active generation from a city; a convoy leg admitted under cap, refused over it; an active march leg priced in credits and debited from the right corp; war-flips-the-queue ordering under contention; determinism (same seed, same allocation). `LOGISTICS.md` § Logistic Points is updated from "still to be argued" to the shipped shape once built.

## Open, flagged not guessed

The two numeric rates (passive city yield, active credit-per-unit-distance) are first-cut calibration constants, not rulings — expect tuning after the live check.

items.title: a Throughput lens renders the reach field as a magnitude, not the binary Reach lens' connection list
items.summary: LOGISTICS.md's LP design calls its planned surface "the Throughput lens, extending Reach" — but LENSES.md's existing 'Reach' lens already means something else (the trade-route connection-list key, DISCOVERY.md). This item builds the LP surface under its own name, Throughput, so the two never collide: a per-tile wash of `tile_reach_cost` scaled by BL-595's cap, magnitude not binary, on the Planetary canvas.
items.design:
## Naming, resolved

Keep 'Reach' as-is (trade routes, connection-list key, unchanged). The new lens is **Throughput** — a distinct strip entry, own glyph (open TODO in `ui::icons` per the Reach lens precedent), reusing the existing `draw_scroll_list_key` chrome only where a list read fits; the primary read is a tile wash, closer kin to the Placement-suitability surface's tile tinting than to Reach's key list.

## What it draws

Per land tile, `tile_reach_cost` (already computed for placement, `logistics.hpp`) scaled against BL-595's per-tick cap: near-anchor tiles read saturated, distant-but-admissible tiles fade, refused tiles (over cap) read in the same tinted-invalid convention the placement-suitability surface uses. **Never triggers the Dijkstra itself** — same constraint `tile_reach_cost`'s const read already carries, this lens is a pure read of the cached field.

## Fold-in

Composites under the fog wash exactly as roads do (BL-185, `fog_dim`, LOGISTICS.md § Roads) — see BL-597, which is the item that specifies the fog interaction precisely rather than assuming it falls out for free.

## Open, flagged for a live look

Bucket count / palette steps for the magnitude gradient are a visual call (Rule 0b) — build a first cut, then a live check picks the final bucketing rather than guessing it here.

items.title: the Throughput lens must read correctly under BOTH fogs — survey (unrevealed) and activity — closing the −1-vs-infinity trap LOGISTICS.md already flags
items.summary: This is the exploration → logistics seam, made concrete: `tile_reach_cost` returns −1 for 'not computed' and infinity for 'computed and unreachable' — a distinction LOGISTICS.md §3 already names as a UI trap. An unsurveyed tile must never leak a throughput number (the survey fog wins outright, matching the existing 'no per-tile data exposed to Lua / no premature reveal' convention); a surveyed-but-unreached tile shows its true cost or an honest 'no network here', never a stale or default value. This is what makes surveying (exploration) and extending the logistics network two readable, separate decisions on the same canvas.
items.design:
## The rule

Draw order, per tile: **survey phase gates first.** `hidden` / `in_transit` / partially-`scanning` tiles (DISCOVERY.md § Geographic fog) render as unrevealed — no Throughput wash at all, same as every other lens today. Only a `surveyed` tile (or a revealed region mid-scan) proceeds to the reach read, where `tile_reach_cost`'s two sentinels are handled explicitly rather than both falling through the same branch: `-1` (not computed — the Dijkstra has not run for this region, e.g. no anchor exists yet anywhere on the body) reads as "no network", distinct from a finite-cost tile and distinct from `infinity` (computed, genuinely unreachable from any anchor) — the second is the refused-tile tint BL-596 already specifies, the first is a third, neutral state that must not be confused with either.

## Why this is its own item, not folded into BL-596

BL-596 specifies what the lens draws once it has a valid cost; this item specifies what it draws when it does not — the fog interaction and the sentinel handling are the exact kind of cross-cutting correctness bug LOGISTICS.md flags happening once already (the cached-path orientation trap, §2). Splitting it keeps BL-596's harness about the gradient and this one's about the fog boundary, so a regression in one does not hide inside the other's golden.

## Verification

Extends `throughput_lens.lua`: a capture on a partially-surveyed body, asserting no reach wash appears past the survey boundary regardless of the underlying (already-computed) field value; a headless case in `logistics_points_harness.cpp` asserting the lens-facing read distinguishes all three states (`-1`, finite, infinity) rather than collapsing `-1` into either neighbour.
